newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN approves three more Iraq contracts, tally at 24.
newsitem.headline: UN approves three more Iraq contracts, tally at 24.

text.p: U.N. oil experts approved three more contracts for Iraq under the oil-for food accord, bringing the total number of contracts approved to 24 since the plan started December 10, U.N. officials said Tuesday.
Although the United Nations has refused to comment on the specifics of the contracts, industry sources said two of the three contracts were for Chevron and Texaco.

A U.N. official said Iraq was nearing the "ceiling" for the amount of oil it was permitted to sell under the terms of the accord, which limits Baghdad to $2 billion of crude sales over the six months of the plan.
"They are getting close to the ceiling. We are not expecting that many more contracts, some but not many," the official said.
Iraq has been refiguring the volumes of some contracts in order to stay under the ceiling in the face of an ever-increasing world oil price.
Texaco said on Monday it was cut back from 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) over six months to 10,000 bpd for the same span.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) also trimmed contracted volumes with Japan's Mitsubishi Corp to 20,000 bpd over six months from 40,000 bpd over three months.
Iraq is also not allowed to sell more than $1 billion worth of crude within each 90-day period of the accord's duration.

The oil sales were approved by the United Nations as a humanitarian exemption to trade sanctions locked on Iraq since it invaded Kuwait in August 1990. Under the deal, Iraq will buy food, medicine and supplies for civilians suffering from those sanctions.
